gauntlet: gate=brainstorming/human-batch
Spec amendments: 2 need your call - from the spec review; applying as recommended reopens no tasks; no phase change.

1. Share retry policy - move retry policy into one owner. Adapters currently disagree about when to retry.
   This is a human call because changing who owns retries is an architecture choice.
   Example: adapter-local retry limits -> one coordinator retry limit
   Reviewer: changing retry ownership needs a human architecture choice
   Impact: retries: each adapter decides its own retry policy -> one shared owner decides retry policy for every adapter
   A) accept - a new retry service owns all retry policies
   B) alt-1 - the existing report coordinator owns the shared retry policy; adapters keep execution
   Custom: <your own answer> - executed as given; may redirect away from the spec
   Recommended: B - reusing the existing coordinator keeps the policy consistent without adding a new service

2. Classify blocked execution - classify exit 126 as blocked rather than failed. Operators need to tell a launch problem apart from a report failure.
   This is a human call because it changes a status that operators see.
   Example: exit 126 = failed -> blocked
   Reviewer: operator-visible status changes need a human decision
   Impact: run status: exit 126 is reported as a failed run -> exit 126 is reported as a blocked run
   A) accept - the spec reads the new text
   Custom: <your own answer> - executed as given; may redirect away from the spec
   Recommended: A - a separate status identifies launch failures

Reply with one line per item: `1. A`, `2. <your own text>`. Bare `1` takes every recommendation.
Standing grant: reply "auto-apply amends" - every later spec amendment in this flow (corrected facts, paths, verification lines, and scope, acceptance-criteria, or public-contract edits alike) applies without asking; only a redraw (changed problem statement, component added, removed, or re-bounded) still stops for you, and the grant never stands in for a spec approval.

Details
crosscut: Design / retries - old: each report adapter owns its retry policy -> new: a new retry service owns all retry policies
crosscut (alt-1): Design / retries - old: each report adapter owns its retry policy -> new: the existing report coordinator owns the shared retry policy; adapters keep execution
exit126: Design / run status - old: exit 126 is failed -> new: exit 126 is blocked

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: No fact moved: both outputs open each item with the plain-words what/why sentence, give the crosscut item A) accept and B) alt-1 with one-line consequences, state Recommended: B and Recommended: A with reasons, use the `1. A` / `2. <your own text>` reply grammar with bare 1 taking every recommendation and no legacy 2: <handle>=<choice> form, and carry one human-call sentence per item (After's 'This is a human call because ...' phrasing is a clean, consistent way to satisfy f6). The one regression worth fixing in After is outside the listed facts: the exit126 option A consequence reads 'the spec reads the new text', which is a template placeholder rather than a real consequence, whereas Before rendered 'exit 126 is reported as blocked'; the wording should require that every lettered option's consequence restate the concrete new behavior (the Accept text or alternative text in plain words), never the placeholder phrase, so that the f2-style one-line-consequence requirement holds for single-option items too.
